text:
alex (PM): FYI ACME just replied to our perf ask. They need 99th percentile latency <= 200ms for chat at bursts of ~200 rps. They asked whether Hosted can handle it or if Dedicated is required. Thoughts on prioritization (latency vs throughput vs cost)?
juan (EngL): 200ms p99 at 200 rps is pretty tight on Hosted unless we increase instances / use larger GPUs. Primary trade is cost vs latency. :thinking:
rachel (ML Eng): We can shrink model sequence length and enable KV cache + prefix caching for chat to reduce repeated context cost. That helps latency but not peak concurrency unless we scale horizontally.
tess (Solutions Eng): ACME is pricing-sensitive. They'll balk at a Dedicated commit without proving value. They asked for an estimate and a short checklist we can show them for a staged rollout.
mila (DevEx): Suggest framing as a 3-step plan: 1) quick config optimizations on Hosted (batching tweaks, cache), 2) run a short load test with customer traffic shape, 3) evaluate Dedicated if Hosted can't meet SLA. We should attach RICE-style scores per step.
alex (PM): Agreed. Can we do rough RICE now to prioritize? I can own Impact and Reach. Juan/rachel please add Effort & Confidence.
juan (EngL): Effort: quick config + autoscaling policy change = ~2 dev-weeks (infra + monitoring). Load test harness and analysis = 1 week. Dedicated onboarding (if needed) = 3-4 weeks plus infra. Confidence = medium.
rachel (ML Eng): Impact: high if we hit ACME's SLA (key logo). Reach: medium — affects other similar mid-market customers. Effort estimate as Juan said. For small perf wins we can try activation of quantized kernels (low risk) -> adds ~3 days.
sam (CTO): Quick note: we should score cost savings per path too. Dedicated may reduce per-token cost at scale but has commitment overhead for the customer. For prioritization, let's add a 'unit economics' column to RICE (not standard, but helps decision).
alex (PM): OK RICE draft in thread: Reach=50 customers, Impact=8/10, Confidence=6/10, Effort=3 (weeks). Using simple RICE formula (Impact * Reach * Confidence / Effort) -> high-level priority. Sam add unit-econ numbers?
sam (CTO): Rough unit econ: Hosted optimizations -> ~$0.005/token saved vs baseline for typical chat pattern. Dedicated -> closer to $0.002/token but requires 3mo commit. I'll have finance run precise numbers.
tess (Solutions Eng): For ACME, requirement matrix they want in contract: p99 <= 200ms, available 99.9%, rollback to previous model if quality/regressions. Can we meet monitoring & alerting criteria within Hosted?
mila (DevEx): We can add route-level latency SLOs in Console, per-route dashboards, and automatic fallback to smaller model variant on overload. Work to wire up alerts is ~3 days.
juan (EngL): Technical risk: concurrency contention on KV cache memory for many concurrent sessions. Fixes: shard cache + response streaming. Effort ~1 week. If we accept slightly higher tail latency (250ms) we can avoid Dedicated for now.
rachel (ML Eng): Also add prompt / eval gating: if we push quantized kernels we should run our eval suite to ensure generation quality stays within thresholds. That gating needs automation (~2 days to plug into pipeline).
alex (PM): Proposal: prioritize 'Hosted optimizations + monitoring + load test' as sprint A (2 weeks), then re-evaluate. If load test fails, escalate to 'Dedicated pilot' as sprint B (4 weeks). Launch criteria: p99<=200ms in load test + unit-econ delta < X (TBD) + quality regression < 1% on eval.
tess (Solutions Eng): Sounds good. I'll prepare a customer-facing rollout plan and contract matrix for ACME.
sam (CTO): Approve moving sprint A to top of infra/ops backlog this sprint. Juan, please estimate exact JIRA tickets.
juan (EngL): Will do. I'll also add a canary policy: route 10% traffic to the optimized config, monitor latency, errors for 48h then ramp.
deploy-bot: deploy request: infra/optimize-hosted-config -> started by juan at 1719000100
alex (PM): Great. Alex signing off — putting this into roadmap board and tagging ACME in the customer asks doc. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
